A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OMAC research, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices. Corresponding methods, experiments and prompt examples can be matched despite reorganization. Reporting inconsistencies limit interpretation of some results, rather than access to comparison material.

before.justification: v1 reports original HumanEval, MMLU and MATH experiments, including single- and multi-dimension optimization, ablations and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, experiments with additional base models, computational-cost measurements and training/test curves.

M1.justification: The five dimensions, two actors, contrastive sampling, alternating optimization and prompt templates are retained. Appendix C.2.4 adds an optional cost-saving variant that evaluates candidates on randomly sampled training subsets instead of the entire training set, tested using 50% per evaluation. This changes candidate scoring without redesigning the core optimizer.

E1.justification: v3 retains HumanEval, MMLU and MATH and adds evaluated MBPP programming tasks and GAIA Level 2 questions (Tables 17–18). GAIA substantially extends coverage to real-world, tool-oriented question answering. SWE-bench and FLICKR30K are discussed or cited, not evaluated by OMAC.

E2.justification: ADAS and AFlow join the comparisons on all three original benchmarks. CAMEL disappears from the HumanEval comparison but appears on MBPP; LLM-Blender disappears from the reasoning performance tables but remains in the new arithmetic-cost comparison. AutoGPT is additionally evaluated on GAIA. These are substantive comparator changes, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: Reported MMLU and HumanEval sample counts change from 68 to 168 and 80 to 180. Appendix C.1 introduces a 3:1:1 train/validation/test split, contradicting its retained benchmark-specific descriptions of equal train/test splits. New settings include three additional base LLMs, 50% training-subset evaluations and a four-iteration training-curve experiment. These are substantial reported protocol changes, but do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing OMAC-C ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity studies and alternating-versus-simultaneous optimization analysis remain. v3 adds computational-efficiency and training-subset tradeoff analyses, robustness evaluations with GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek-V2.5 and Qwen-2.5-72B, and paired training/test curves examining overfitting (Appendices C.2.4–C.2.7).

E5.justification: Both versions specify three repetitions and reporting means and standard deviations; retained performance curves keep their error bars. v3 documents no increased repeat count, new seed information, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure. Additional results do not establish a changed statistical estimation practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial benchmark, model, cost and training-curve results. Arithmetic Tables 3–7 revise numerical values: Str-1 changes from 33.06±1.62 to 33.34±1.45. Table 3 changes SE from 28.31±2.01 to 28.72±1.75, the value previously assigned to LLM-Blender. Original HumanEval/MMLU OMAC scores and Figures 4–7 curve points are retained. Given the conflicting protocol descriptions, revised scores cannot be interpreted as demonstrated same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: The formal agent and collaboration definitions and threshold-based sampling mathematics remain unchanged. v3 adds an intuitive information-flow graph explanation and explicitly defers theoretical guarantees; it introduces no formal graph derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The five-dimensional framework, two actors and iterative joint optimization remain the central contributions. The introduction removes v1's 'in most scenarios' qualification from the single-dimension superiority claim, a limited strengthening, although Section 4.1 still qualifies improvements as occurring 'in most cases'.

C2.justification: v1's brief discussion of LLM dependence, variance and computational demands becomes extensive interpretation in Appendix D. v3 argues that iterative feedback mitigates weak candidates and reasoning bias, interprets training/test alignment as absence of overfitting, and discusses efficiency tradeoffs. It newly specifies the current focus on flat MAS, adaptations needed for centralized systems, and untested extensions involving memory, retrieval and theoretical guarantees.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a code-repository pointer in the abstract and Appendix E.1, directing readers there for other task prompts. It adds the GAIA agent configuration, explicitly states that validation-set tuning was not performed, and quantifies API calls and dollar costs where v1 mainly discussed computational demands qualitatively. Existing detailed prompt templates remain. Repository accessibility and contents cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands positioning beyond the earlier emphasis on DyLAN, comparing gradient-based and non-gradient approaches including ADAS, AFlow, G-Designer, MaAS, Spiral and MHGPO. Appendix D.3 acknowledges conceptual precedents for the actors and emphasizes integration within a unified framework. Other additions address tool use, cost and centralized MAS, while several earlier general-agent references are removed.

P1.justification: The supplementary narrative is substantially reorganized: expanded related work becomes Appendix A, the short limitations section is rewritten into six discussion subsections before the prompt appendix, and ablation and multi-dimension subsections exchange order. The title changes from 'Broad' to 'Holistic', while introduction, methodological motivation, related-work prose and conclusion receive revisions. Much core method and prompt wording remains intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns. Figures 1–3 are reformatted or redrawn, and Figures 4–7 add DyLAN reference lines and rescaled vertical axes while retaining their OMAC trajectories. v3 adds nine experimental tables and Figure 8, swaps the first two benchmark tables, and relocates the existing prompt tables as Tables 19–20.

improvement.justification: The added optimization baselines, broader evaluations, quantitative cost analyses and code pointer address important weaknesses in v1. However, v3 introduces contradictory split descriptions and changes sample counts while retaining earlier scores, leaving their experimental provenance unclear; Table 3 also assigns SE the value previously reported for LLM-Blender without explanation. The gains in breadth coexist with material losses in reporting clarity, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
